rows.description: An observer sees a neighbourhood spending heavily on decorations, loud music or donations demanded by committees. Real community joy can sit alongside quiet worry about cost, noise and being forced to contribute.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult visits a friend's home on their festival, brings sweets and respects their customs without needing to share the beliefs. Shared joy builds trust in a mixed neighbourhood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: joy, admiration, trust

rows.description: A toddler at a naming or first rice-eating ceremony is dressed up, held by many hands and photographed. The child remembers the mood and faces, not the ritual; the ceremony marks the family's welcome.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child sees a younger cousin's naming or mundan ceremony and asks why so many people came. The event teaches that a life belongs to a wider circle of family, faith and community.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A boy at an upanayana or a child at a similar rite in another faith feels proud, nervous and watched. A rite marks a new duty and can also be confusing if the meaning is not explained.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, confusion, pride

rows.description: A child sees that a rite is given to some children and not others, for example by gender or family. Feeling left out is honest, and calm adults explain the tradition while listening to the child's hurt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Coming of age and body changes [Receiver]
rows.description: A girl who is told to observe restrictions after her first period may feel shamed, protected or important all at once. Health facts and respect should replace secrecy and stigma.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult at a big wedding feels joy, pressure and exhaustion as relatives assess dress, food and customs. Seeing the ceremony as a marker of a new stage helps separate real meaning from show.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult performs last rites for a grandparent and feels grief, duty and numbness at once. Ritual gives shape to loss, and being allowed to cry is as important as doing the tasks right.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: sadness, grief, detachment

rows.description: A young adult keeps rites that carry meaning, adapts some, and skips those that hurt or exclude, explaining kindly. Change offered with respect for the elders' feelings is heard better than open rejection.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
